column1: # bare-sort-triage.tsv — the loop's memory of which bare `.sort()` calls (no
# comparator) have already been JUDGED, so find-bare-sort.mjs --check can stay
# green on the healthy tree and fail ONLY on a NEW, untriaged bare sort.
# A bare `.sort()` orders elements as STRINGS (UTF-16 code units). That is:
#   • a BUG when the receiver holds raw NUMBERS  ([1,10,2].sort() → wrong order)
#   • SAFE when it holds genuine strings, fixed-width keys, or ISO dates
#     (lexical order == the intended order), or when the result is used only as
#     a canonical/equality key where ANY deterministic order is fine.
#   STATUS = SAFE (judged a non-bug) | BUG (open — fix it)
# The key is the whitespace-stripped receiver expression (not file:line), so a
# row survives edits that move the call. Change the receiver text → reads as NEW
# again (re-review), the safe direction. Add a row the moment you judge a site.
